title: Scheme-base-change test for universal closedness of representable stack maps
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Stacks, Deligne--Mumford stacks, algebraic spaces and 2-fibre products have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Representable by algebraic spaces means that every scheme base change is equivalent to an algebraic space. Properties of such maps are tested on these algebraic-space base changes. The point space $|\mathcal X|$ consists of field-valued [def-weil-field] objects up to isomorphism and common field extension, with topology detected by a smooth scheme atlas. Let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a representable-by-algebraic-spaces morphism of Deligne--Mumford stacks over $S$. The following conditions are equivalent. (a) For every morphism $\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y$ from an algebraic stack, the point-space map $|\mathcal Z\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X|\to|\mathcal Z|$ is closed. (b) For every scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$, the algebraic-space morphism $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X\to T$ is universally closed. For a map of algebraic spaces, universally closed means that after every algebraic-space base change its point-space map is closed; its point spaces use the same field-point equivalence and etale-atlas topology. If $\mathcal X$ and $\mathcal Y$ are algebraic spaces, these conditions are equivalent to ordinary universal closedness of $f$. Here an algebraic stack is a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] surjective scheme atlas; the other stack conventions are those already specified.

source.place: Tag 0512 (lemma-characterize-representable-universally-closed); equivalence with testing schemes: Tag 0CL3 (lemma-universally-closed-local); spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03XD (lemma-characterize-representable-universally-closed).

proof.text: Assume (a). An algebraic space is an algebraic stack when viewed as a discrete fibred groupoid: its sheaf condition gives descent, its diagonal is representable, and its surjective etale scheme atlas is smooth by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Fix a scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$ and an algebraic space $W\to T$. Representability makes $X_T=T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ an algebraic space. Its base change $W\times_T X_T$ is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The canonical equivalence $W\times_T(T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X)\simeq W\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ forgets the redundant $T$-object and composes its identifying isomorphism; its inverse inserts the image of the $W$-object in $T$ and its identity. These functors preserve the projection to $W$ and are inverse up to the displayed identifying isomorphism. By [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology] they induce inverse homeomorphisms of point spaces. Apply (a) to $W\to\mathcal Y$: this base-change projection is closed for every $W\to T$. This is precisely universal closedness of $X_T\to T$, proving (b).

source.place: Tag 0512 (lemma-characterize-representable-universally-closed), implication (2) to (1); expanded for algebraic-space base changes.

proof.text: Assume (b), and fix an arbitrary algebraic stack $\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y$. The Deligne--Mumford stacks $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ are algebraic stacks: their diagonals are representable by algebraic spaces and their surjective etale scheme atlases are smooth by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Put $\mathcal P=\mathcal Z\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$; it is an algebraic stack by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products] applied to $\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y\leftarrow\mathcal X$. Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $v:V\to\mathcal Z$. Put $E=V\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$, an algebraic space by representability of $f$. The projection $g:E\to V$ is universally closed by (b), hence closed on point spaces by taking the identity base change. The object-triple construction identifies $V\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal P$ with $E$: an object $(u,(z,x,\alpha),\beta)$, where $\beta:v(u)\xrightarrow{\sim}z$ and $\alpha:k(z)\xrightarrow{\sim}f(x)$ for $k:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y$, maps to $(u,x,\alpha\circ k(\beta))$. The inverse inserts $z=v(u)$ and $\beta=1$; the original $\beta$ gives the isomorphism back. An arrow $(a,b,c)$ obeys $b\beta=\beta' v(a)$ and $f(c)\alpha=\alpha' k(b)$; send it to $(a,c)$. Its compatibility follows from $f(c)\alpha k(\beta)=\alpha' k(b\beta)=\alpha' k(\beta')kv(a)$. The inverse sends $(a,c)$ to $(a,v(a),c)$. These formulas commute with pullback and preserve both projections. Write $r:|E|\to|\mathcal P|$, $h:|\mathcal P|\to|\mathcal Z|$ and $q=|v|$. By [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology], $r$ is continuous and $q$ is a surjective quotient map (closedness is detected by its inverse image). The square satisfies $h r=q|g|$.

source.place: Tag 0512 (lemma-characterize-representable-universally-closed), first paragraph and displayed diagram.

proof.text: The map $|E|\to |V|\times_{|\mathcal Z|}|\mathcal P|$ is onto. Indeed choose field-valued representatives of $u\in|V|$ and $p\in|\mathcal P|$ with the same image in $|\mathcal Z|$. By the field-point equivalence specified in [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology], over a common field extension their images in $\mathcal Z$ are isomorphic. The two extended objects together with this isomorphism are exactly an object of $V\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal P\simeq E$, and its projections represent $u$ and $p$. Consequently for any subset $B\subseteq|\mathcal P|$ one has $q^{-1}(h(B))=|g|(r^{-1}(B))$: the inclusion from right to left is commutativity, and the reverse inclusion follows by lifting the pair $(u,p)$ for a point $p\in B$ mapping to $q(u)$. This proves the point-lifting assertion directly, without identifying a point space with a set-theoretic fibre product.

source.place: Tag 0512, point-space surjectivity assertion; stacks-properties.tex Tag 04XH (lemma-points-cartesian), the common-field-extension argument.

proof.text: Let $B\subseteq|\mathcal P|$ be closed. Continuity of $r$ makes $r^{-1}(B)$ closed in $|E|$. Since $|g|$ is closed, the equality of the preceding step makes $q^{-1}(h(B))$ closed in $|V|$. The atlas quotient criterion in [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology] then says that $h(B)$ is closed in $|\mathcal Z|$. Thus $h$ is a closed map for every algebraic stack $\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y$, proving (a).

source.place: Tag 0512, descent of closedness at the end of implication (1) to (2).

proof.text: Finally suppose $\mathcal X=X$ and $\mathcal Y=Y$ are algebraic spaces. If (a) holds, restrict its test stacks to algebraic spaces $W\to Y$. Their 2-fibre products are the ordinary sheaf fibre products: all groupoids are discrete, so the isomorphism in an object triple is exactly equality. By [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology] the point topologies are the usual ones, and this gives ordinary universal closedness of $X\to Y$. Conversely, suppose $X\to Y$ is universally closed as an algebraic-space map. For each scheme $T\to Y$ and algebraic space $W\to T$, the algebraic-space fibre products exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and $W\times_T(T\times_YX)\cong W\times_YX$ over $W$: forgetting $T$ and inserting its prescribed image are inverse on sections. Its projection is closed by the assumed ordinary universal closedness. Hence $T\times_YX\to T$ is universally closed, which is (b); the equivalence just proved gives (a).
